property.statement: W27=W32 XOR W33, W23=W33 XOR W35 and W3=W27 XOR SB(ROTL8(W23)) XOR RCON4.
property.quantifier: For every standard AES-192 expanded key. This is an exact word dependency; the printed footnote byte example is assessed separately.
property.scope: Three distant schedule words determine whitening word3. In the specified eight-round attack, the bridge saves8 guessed bits on top of24 other schedule bits.

parameters.name: Distant supplied words
parameters.meaning: Columns0,1,3 of k7 in the paper's zero-based convention.

parameters.name: Attack guessing reduction
parameters.meaning: 24bits from nearby schedule relations plus8bits from the distant bridge.

parameters.name: External related-key applications
parameters.reported: First variant data2^64.5→2^64.43; other two only qualitative small benefits.
parameters.meaning: Section5.2.2 studies two-related-secret-key ZWZF07 attacks. First two whitening bytes can be bridged, other variants one; no general eight-bit whole-attack speedup or extra exact vector.

validation.description: 512 valid random AES-192 schedules and the expanded Eq1 family pass. A separate valid-key pair witnesses the printed footnote coordinate problem.

field_conflicts.label: Key-bridge footnote byte coordinates
field_conflicts.description: The word recurrence is verified, but footnote8 lists k7 bytes0,4,7,15. For whitening byte15 used in Section7, the recurrence instead requires k7[3],k7[7],k7[4],k7[12]. A local pair of valid AES-192 schedules preserves the four footnote bytes and changes whitening byte15.
